source_text: Klagel. Jerem. 4, 1. Τῆς νῦν παρούσης τετάρτης στοιχειώσεως ἀρχόμενος τὸν περὶ τῶν ἐπιφανῶν ἐξαιρέτως ἐπανέλαβε Θρῆνον, ἠμαυρῶσθαι λέγων τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν ἐκκεχυμένου τε δίκην ὕδατος ἠφανίσθαι.
pass_a_gloss: [Pass A] Beginning the fourth alphabetic sequence now present, he has taken up again especially the lament about the illustrious ones, saying the brilliance has been dimmed and has vanished poured out like water.
pass_b_english: Beginning the fourth alphabetic sequence now present, he has taken up again especially the lament about the illustrious ones, saying the brilliance has been dimmed and has vanished poured out like water.

choices.why: Origen allegorizes God’s word as sword at Lam 4:9.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Origen’s Greek Lamentations fragments. Sense checked against Klostermann GCS III. Modern English not copied. OET = no previous English translation.

apparatus.note: Source Greek OCR-noisy; restorations disclosed in translator_notes.
